topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: To satisfy Wis. Stat. 240.10(1) so a broker can later sue to collect a sales commission, the signed writing generally must state:
choice_a: Only the commission percentage, with all other terms left to be agreed later
choice_b: The buyer's name and mortgage lender, but not the commission amount
choice_c: Nothing more than the broker's license number
choice_d: A description of the property, the sale price, the commission amount, and the time period within which the broker is to procure a buyer or seller
explanation: Wis. Stat. 240.10(1) voids a commission contract unless it describes the property, states the sale price, states the commission amount, and states the period during which the broker is to procure a buyer or seller.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Wis. Stat. 240.10(2) extends the same type of written-agreement requirement to a broker's commission for procuring a lease when:
choice_a: The lease term exceeds 3 years
choice_b: The lease is for a single-family home
choice_c: The tenant is a corporation
choice_d: The lease includes an option to purchase
explanation: Wis. Stat. 240.10(2) applies the writing requirement to a broker's commission for procuring a lease with a term exceeding 3 years, requiring the property description, rent terms, lease length, commission amount, procurement period, and the payor's signature.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Under Wis. Stat. 240.10, a commission contract hiring someone merely to locate a type of property (rather than a specific parcel) is treated differently in that it:
choice_a: Is completely exempt from being in writing
choice_b: Need not describe the specific property, unlike a standard commission contract written for a particular parcel
choice_c: May be enforced even if unsigned by the payor
choice_d: Applies only to commercial property
explanation: Wis. Stat. 240.10 excuses a contract to locate a type of property from the property-description requirement, since there is no specific parcel to describe -- the other requirements (writing, signature by the payor) still apply.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: In a buyer agency/tenant representation agreement, the same signature logic that Wis. Stat. 240.10 applies to listing contracts points to which party's signature as the one that obligates payment of a commission?
choice_a: The seller in whatever transaction eventually closes
choice_b: The listing firm's broker
choice_c: The buyer/tenant client, as the party contracting with the firm and obligated under that agreement
choice_d: The Real Estate Examining Board
explanation: Wis. Stat. 240.10 requires the writing to be signed by the person obligated to pay the commission; under a buyer agency/tenant representation agreement, that contracting, obligated party is the buyer/tenant client.
source_note: Wis. Stat. 240.10; hedge: how buyer-agency commissions are ultimately funded (e.g., via seller-offered cooperative compensation) has shifted industry practice nationally since 2024, but this question addresses only the contract-law signature/payor principle, not current compensation-disclosure mechanics.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: REEB 16.02(3) defines an 'exclusive right to sell listing' as a written listing contract that:
choice_a: Allows the owner to sell without paying any commission whenever the owner personally finds the buyer
choice_b: May be given to multiple firms at the same time
choice_c: Applies only to commercial property
choice_d: Makes a firm the exclusive agent to sell the property for a specific period and entitles the firm to a commission regardless of whether the property is sold by the owner, the firm, or anyone else
explanation: REEB 16.02(3) defines an exclusive right to sell listing as a written listing contract making the firm the exclusive agent for a specific period, entitling the firm to a commission no matter who sells the property.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: REEB 16.02(2) defines an 'exclusive agency listing' as:
choice_a: A written listing agreement with all the elements of an exclusive right to sell listing, except that the owner keeps the right to sell the property personally without owing the listing firm a commission
choice_b: A listing that may be given to any number of firms
choice_c: A listing under which the firm never earns a commission
choice_d: A listing limited to a single named buyer
explanation: REEB 16.02(2) defines an exclusive agency listing as containing all the elements of an exclusive right to sell listing except that the owner retains the right to sell without owing the listing broker a commission.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: REEB 16.02(4) defines an 'open listing' as a written listing agreement that:
choice_a: May be given to only one firm at a time
choice_b: May be given to any number of firms, with the first firm to secure a buyer under its terms earning the commission
choice_c: Automatically entitles every firm holding it to a share of the commission
choice_d: Is not permitted under Wisconsin law
explanation: REEB 16.02(4) defines an open listing as a written listing agreement that may be given to any number of firms, with the commission earned by whichever firm first secures a buyer under the listing's terms.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: REEB 16.02(4m) defines a 'one-party listing' as a written listing contract with all the elements of an exclusive right to sell listing, except that:
choice_a: No commission is ever owed under the listing
choice_b: It may only be used for rental property
choice_c: The firm earns a commission only if the property is sold to one or more specific parties identified in the listing contract
choice_d: It automatically renews every year without a new signature
explanation: REEB 16.02(4m) defines a one-party listing as carrying all the elements of an exclusive right to sell listing, except the firm's commission entitlement is limited to a sale to a specific party or parties named in the contract.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: How does a one-party listing under REEB 16.02(4m) differ from a standard exclusive right to sell listing under REEB 16.02(3)?
choice_a: A one-party listing has no time limit while an exclusive right to sell listing must expire within 30 days
choice_b: A one-party listing cannot be in writing
choice_c: There is no meaningful difference between the two
choice_d: A one-party listing limits the firm's commission entitlement to a sale to one or more named parties, while an exclusive right to sell listing entitles the firm to a commission no matter who buys
explanation: A one-party listing is a narrowed version of an exclusive right to sell listing: it shares the same structure but restricts the firm's commission entitlement to a sale to the specific party or parties identified in the contract.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: REEB 16.02(1m) defines a 'buyer agency/tenant representation agreement' as a written agency agreement that:
choice_a: Authorizes a firm to provide brokerage services to the client for procuring an interest in property and sets the terms under which the firm may earn a commission
choice_b: Automatically makes the buyer a subagent of the seller's firm
choice_c: Applies only when the buyer is purchasing a condominium
choice_d: Waives the firm's duty of confidentiality to the buyer
explanation: REEB 16.02(1m) defines a buyer agency/tenant representation agreement as a written agency agreement authorizing a firm to provide brokerage services for the client's procurement of an interest in property, and setting the commission terms.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: The WB-36 form combines 'buyer agency' and 'tenant representation' into one standard agreement because REEB 16.02(1m) defines the underlying agency agreement in terms of:
choice_a: A requirement that every buyer must also lease space before purchasing
choice_b: Procuring 'an interest in property,' a concept broad enough to cover both a purchase (buyer agency) and a lease (tenant representation)
choice_c: A rule limiting tenant representation to commercial tenants only
choice_d: A formal merger of the WB-1 and WB-4 forms
explanation: Because REEB 16.02(1m) frames the agreement around procuring 'an interest in property' -- which includes both buying and leasing -- one standard form (WB-36) can serve both a purchasing client (buyer agency) and a leasing client (tenant representation).

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Among the categories of forms REEB 16.03 approves for licensee use, which category is prepared by the State Bar of Wisconsin?
choice_a: Buyer agency agreements
choice_b: Listing contracts
choice_c: Forms for deeds, mortgages, mortgage notes, truth-in-lending disclosures, and land contracts
choice_d: Offers to purchase
explanation: REEB 16.03 approves State Bar of Wisconsin forms covering deeds, mortgages, mortgage notes, truth-in-lending disclosures, land contracts, and related conveyance documents, distinct from the board's own listing and offer forms.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: REEB 16.03 also approves a category of forms drawn from:
choice_a: Federal tax law exclusively
choice_b: Out-of-state condominium associations only
choice_c: The board's own listing and buyer agency library only
choice_d: The Uniform Commercial Code, for use in transactions involving personal property or fixtures
explanation: REEB 16.03 approves a set of Uniform Commercial Code forms for licensee use, alongside State Bar forms, out-of-state forms, government/tribal forms, and property management agreements.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: REEB 16.03 permits a Wisconsin licensee to use an out-of-state real estate form when:
choice_a: The transaction involves property in that other state and the form is customarily used there
choice_b: The client simply requests it for a Wisconsin transaction
choice_c: No Wisconsin-approved form exists for any purpose whatsoever
choice_d: The firm's broker personally drafted the out-of-state form
explanation: REEB 16.03 approves out-of-state forms for real estate transactions occurring in other states, conditioned on the form being customarily used there -- it is not a general substitute for Wisconsin-approved forms in Wisconsin transactions.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Besides State Bar, UCC, out-of-state, and property management forms, REEB 16.03 also approves forms prepared by:
choice_a: Any individual licensee, without board review
choice_b: Governmental, quasi-governmental, and tribal entities
choice_c: Out-of-state multiple listing services only
choice_d: Title insurance underwriters exclusively
explanation: REEB 16.03's approved-forms categories include forms prepared by governmental, quasi-governmental, and tribal entities, in addition to State Bar, UCC, out-of-state, and property management agreement forms.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: REEB 16.04 permits a licensee to use a listing or buyer agency form that is NOT a board-approved form when:
choice_a: The client verbally agrees to waive the approved-forms requirement
choice_b: The transaction value exceeds a set dollar threshold
choice_c: The form was drafted by a party to the transaction or by an attorney, and the drafter's name is imprinted on the form before use
choice_d: The licensee has more than 10 years of experience
explanation: REEB 16.04 allows use of a non-board-approved contractual form when it is drafted by a party or an attorney and the drafter's name is imprinted on the form before use -- experience level and transaction size are irrelevant.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Beyond using attorney- or party-drafted forms with the drafter identified, REEB 16.04 also allows a licensee to:
choice_a: Draft an entirely new standardized listing contract for board approval without submitting it for review
choice_b: Refuse to use any form the board has approved, at the licensee's sole discretion
choice_c: Charge the client a separate fee for drafting legal language into the form
choice_d: Permit the parties or their attorneys to draft agreements embodying terms the parties have negotiated
explanation: REEB 16.04 additionally allows a licensee to permit parties or their attorneys to draft agreements that embody terms the parties have negotiated, alongside the drafter-identified-form exception.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: In addition to barring legal advice, REEB 16.05 also prohibits a licensee from:
choice_a: Charging a separate fee for completing or explaining an approved listing or buyer agency form
choice_b: Delivering a fully signed copy of the form to the client
choice_c: Keeping a copy of the executed form in the firm's file
choice_d: Using the same approved form for more than one transaction
explanation: REEB 16.05 bars a licensee from charging a separate fee for completing or explaining an approved form, on top of its prohibition on giving legal advice about the form's provisions.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: When a firm reproduces an approved listing or buyer agency form for its own use, REEB 16.06 requires the reproduction to display:
choice_a: The individual agent's personal cell phone number only
choice_b: The reproducing firm's name, address, and telephone number
choice_c: The buyer's employer
choice_d: The date the form was originally printed by a commercial printer
explanation: REEB 16.06 requires a firm reproducing an approved form to indicate the reproducing firm's name, address, and telephone number on the reproduction.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: REEB 16.06 requires that, when a firm reproduces an approved form, the board's approval statement and date must:
choice_a: Be removed to shorten the document
choice_b: Be updated to reflect the date of reproduction
choice_c: Remain unchanged from the original approved form
choice_d: Be replaced with the firm's own internal certification
explanation: REEB 16.06 requires the board's approval statement and date to be retained unchanged whenever a firm reproduces an approved form -- it may not be updated, removed, or substituted.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: When reproducing an approved form, REEB 16.06 allows a firm to change only:
choice_a: The order in which the contract clauses appear
choice_b: The commission-calculation formula printed on the form
choice_c: The board's approval statement
choice_d: The margins and font, without altering the line numbering, page format, or content
explanation: REEB 16.06 limits permitted formatting changes on a reproduced approved form to margins and font -- line numbering, page format, and substantive content must stay as approved.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: If a firm wants to add a term to an approved listing or buyer agency form that the standard form doesn't already address, REEB 16.06 requires the firm to:
choice_a: Use the form's provided blank lines or an addendum, rather than adding new content lines to the approved form itself
choice_b: Retype the entire form with the new term inserted wherever convenient
choice_c: Attach a handwritten note to the signed original with no other formality
choice_d: Seek the board's approval before every individual transaction that needs the added term
explanation: REEB 16.06 confines added terms to the form's own provided blank lines or a properly used addendum -- a firm may not insert new content lines directly into the body of an approved form.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: WB-1, the Wisconsin REALTORS Association standard listing form central to this track, is titled:
choice_a: Residential Offer to Purchase
choice_b: Residential Listing Contract - Exclusive Right to Sell
choice_c: Buyer Agency/Tenant Representation Agreement
choice_d: Commercial Listing Contract
explanation: WB-1 is the WRA's Residential Listing Contract - Exclusive Right to Sell, the standard exclusive-right-to-sell listing form for non-condominium residential property.
source_note: WRA Forms Library (wra.org), independently verified via live fetch for this backfill pass

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: WB-4 is currently the Wisconsin REALTORS Association's:
choice_a: Multiple Listing Service membership agreement
choice_b: Vacant Land Listing Contract
choice_c: Residential Condominium Listing Contract - Exclusive Right to Sell
choice_d: Amendment to Offer to Purchase
explanation: WB-4 is the WRA's Residential Condominium Listing Contract - Exclusive Right to Sell -- the condominium counterpart to WB-1, not an MLS membership document. It exists because condo sales involve association documents and assessments that a standard residential listing does not address.
source_note: WRA Forms Library (wra.org), independently verified via live fetch for this backfill pass -- note: WB-4 is sometimes assumed to relate to 'multiple listing' participation based on its listing-contract family name, but its actual current subject is condominium property, paralleling WB-1 for non-condo residential listings.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: WB-36, the form referenced alongside WB-1 and WB-4 in this track, is titled:
choice_a: Residential Offer to Purchase
choice_b: Cancellation Agreement and Mutual Release
choice_c: Commercial Offer to Purchase
choice_d: Buyer Agency/Tenant Representation Agreement
explanation: WB-36 is the WRA's Buyer Agency/Tenant Representation Agreement, the standard form implementing the REEB 16.02(1m) buyer agency/tenant representation agreement definition.
source_note: WRA Forms Library (wra.org), independently verified via live fetch for this backfill pass

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: A firm has a landlord's attorney draft a custom tenant representation agreement but does not print the attorney's name on the form before using it. Under REEB 16.04, this:
choice_a: Violates REEB 16.04, because a non-board-approved form drafted by a party or attorney may be used only if the drafter's name is imprinted on it before use
choice_b: Is permitted because attorneys are automatically exempt from the approved-forms rule
choice_c: Is a problem only if the landlord later objects to the form
choice_d: Is permitted as long as the firm charges no separate fee for the form
explanation: REEB 16.04's exception for non-approved, attorney- or party-drafted forms is conditioned on the drafter's name being imprinted on the form before use; omitting that identification takes the form outside the exception.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: A firm reprints the WB-1 listing contract in its own template but strips out the board's approval date to make the layout look cleaner. Under REEB 16.06, this:
choice_a: Is allowed, because the approval date is purely optional decoration
choice_b: Violates REEB 16.06, which requires the board's approval statement and date to remain unchanged on any reproduced approved form
choice_c: Is required, since outdated approval dates could confuse clients
choice_d: Only matters for condominium listing forms, not WB-1
explanation: REEB 16.06 requires that the board's approval statement and date be retained unchanged when a firm reproduces an approved form -- removing it for aesthetic reasons is a violation regardless of which approved form is involved.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: A seller signs a one-party listing under REEB 16.02(4m) naming only Buyer X. If Buyer Y, who is not named in the contract, later purchases the property during the listing term through the firm's marketing efforts, the listing firm:
choice_a: Is automatically entitled to the full commission regardless of who buys
choice_b: Must split the commission with Buyer Y's agent regardless of the listing's terms
choice_c: Is not entitled to a commission under the one-party listing, because it obligates the seller to pay only if the named party (Buyer X) is the purchaser
choice_d: Automatically converts the contract into an exclusive right to sell listing
explanation: A one-party listing under REEB 16.02(4m) narrows commission entitlement to a sale to the specific party or parties named in the contract; a sale to an unnamed buyer does not trigger the commission under that listing.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: A broker performs substantial work marketing a property under only an oral agreement with the owner to pay a 6% commission. When the property sells, the broker sues the owner for the commission. Under Wis. Stat. 240.10, the broker's suit:
choice_a: Automatically succeeds because the broker performed substantial work
choice_b: Succeeds only if the sale price exceeded a set statutory threshold
choice_c: Is decided solely by the Real Estate Examining Board rather than a court
choice_d: Generally fails, because the statute requires a written, signed listing agreement before an action to recover a real estate commission may be brought
explanation: Wis. Stat. 240.10 bars an action to recover a real estate commission unless the listing agreement is in writing and signed by the payor -- an oral agreement, however much work the broker performed under it, generally will not support the suit.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Both an exclusive agency listing and an open listing can result in the owner selling without owing a commission if the owner alone procures the buyer. Under REEB 16.02, the key difference is that an open listing, unlike an exclusive agency listing:
choice_a: May be given to any number of firms at the same time, with only the firm that actually procures the buyer earning a commission
choice_b: Cannot be terminated by the owner once signed
choice_c: Requires MLS participation by the listing firm
choice_d: Is not permitted to be in writing under REEB 16.02
explanation: An exclusive agency listing is held by only one firm at a time; an open listing under REEB 16.02(4) may be given to any number of firms simultaneously, with commission earned only by whichever firm actually procures the buyer.
